item.title: XR devs, here’s a detail to keep in mind when building gaze interactions for Meta VR Glasses: looking at a button doesn’
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
XR devs, here’s a detail to keep in mind when building gaze interactions for Meta VR Glasses: looking at a button doesn’t necessarily mean you want to activate it! 👀
Keep hover feedback subtle, give targets enough size and spacing, and reveal additional options after an intentional action, such as a pinch. Moving or expanding your UI just because someone looks at it can make it harder to use.
Small details like these can make the experience feel so much better! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2114532245495250952/video/1
Take a look at all of these best practices in more detail here 👇 https://developers.meta.com/vr/design/eyes-best-practices/

item.title: 📣 XR devs, here are few more great tips!
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
📣 XR devs, here are few more great tips!
Virtual shadows and lighting can make your MR content feel like it actually belongs in your room. Think of a character casting a shadow on your floor or a virtual flame lighting up your desk. Small details, but they can make such a big difference! Meta’s MRUK Passthrough Relighting sample shows how to build these effects in Unity.
- Use MRUK room data to align effects with floors, walls, and furniture.
- Add EffectMesh geometry to receive virtual shadows and highlights.
- Combine directional-light shadows with point-light highlights.
- Compare Scene Model geometry with Global Mesh to see what works best for your environment.
- Tune shadow quality and profile on-device. Try blob shadows for a less expensive alternative. https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2113767854638342414/photo/1
💡 Few useful resources to help you with the implementation in your own games:
- Guide and visuals: https://developers.meta.com/vr/documentation/unity/unity-passthrough-relighting
- GitHub Sample project: https://github.com/oculus-samples/Unity-MRUtilityKitSample

item.title: This is exciting for XR devs!
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
This is exciting for XR devs! Khronos has published new OpenXR Spatial Container extensions for apps that can share your space and switch into fully immersive experiences.
What interests me is the common API that game engines can integrate across compatible platforms! 🙌
- Switch between bounded and fully immersive modes - Support multitasking with multiple apps - Create multiple spatial containers within an app - Let the system manage container positioning - Render into containers using OpenXR composition layers
The specs and sample are published; availability depends on engine and runtime support. https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2113726842779861304/video/1
Full announcement from Khronos 👇 https://www.khronos.org/blog/openxr-spatial-containers

item.title: I’ve been quietly building a new Hand Pose Baking tool for Meta VR Glasses that also works with Quest devices.
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
I’ve been quietly building a new Hand Pose Baking tool for Meta VR Glasses that also works with Quest devices. I had a lot of issues when I started: one object taking 2–3 minutes to bake, fingers going through meshes, and poses that just didn’t look quite right.
💡But why do this? Well, I think realistic hand grab poses with more variety can make interactions feel more engaging and natural, especially if we can generate them without any manual work.
So far, I’m getting better results. It’s not perfect, but honestly, the improvements are so good! It now takes just 2–3 seconds to bake one object. https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2112800102712775157/video/1

item.title: I’ve been a dev for decades, but recently I’ve developed a huge passion for agentic workflows.
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
I’ve been a dev for decades, but recently I’ve developed a huge passion for agentic workflows. Combining the speed of these tools with my experience honestly feels like I can clone myself and have superpowers!
The talented @AshrayPai shares that same passion and sat down with me for an interview at Meta Connect 2026. Hear what he had to say! 👇
引用 @MetaVRDevs："It's a human who has to put on the headset and see if your interaction is natural or not."
That's @AshrayPai answering a question about agentic tools from Meta developer advocate @Dilmerv in episode 1 of Unscripted, our new series where a developer and a Meta developer advocate candidly take turns answering questions about building on Meta platforms.
In this episode, Ashray and Dilmer shared how they use agentic tools to accelerate VR development. Scaffolding, SDK and package setup, debugging and test runs all go to Ashray's agents. Comfort and interaction quality stay with him, in the headset. He sums it up as anything that needs testing can go to an agent, and anything that requires judging needs a human.
Watch episode 1 to hear how both of them use agentic tools in their day-to-day workflows and stay tuned for more episodes 👉 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZK0-t56JggU #MetaVR #MetaVRGlasses #DevTools #AICoding https://x.com/MetaVRDevs/status/2112667703203021055/video/1

item.title: Took a look at the Deckard-Plano (Micro-OLED Frame) stuff… after waking up to pure panic
item.dc:creator: SadlyItsBradley
item.content:encoded:
Took a look at the Deckard-Plano (Micro-OLED Frame) stuff… after waking up to pure panic
Yeah it’s in there. And they do a lot of wacky things to make it possible… with the current 8 Gen 3 chip
They even pair it with the upcoming hotswappable battery headstrap by default
In my opinion, that’s probably required due to power consumption.. And while I would love to say “True Deckard soon,” I genuinely think they’re better off waiting a bit more for the Compute module to upgraded to a newer chip, with these Micro-OLED displays that ALSO need new optics
You could argue that it’s only for streaming PCVR, but I disagree. Valve built just enough of FrameOS to support the Spatial Computing usecase to where people can do some amazing things with a Linux PC on their Face. And while that’s still hella buggy, and taped together.. that’s just software waiting to be fixed
When you switch to Micro-OLED, you get way better visuals. But lose VR gaming focused aspects such as FoV and motion clarity. BUT it still is a greater experience, in my opinion, for many other things
Valve positions the current Frame as a way to play the entire 2D game library. Verified titles for those is quickly growing way faster than VR titles
But frankly, the current display/optics setup truly doesn’t make that usecase more enjoyable. A slightly lower FoV + Micro-OLED system definitely would
But even with the foveal magic they’re introducing here in the code, that doesn’t solve the heat and performance problems even with streaming. The 8 Gen 3 isn’t THAT much better than the chip in the Samsung Galaxy XR. Which uses a lot of these same tricks on an XR2+ Gen 2
That headset throttles a lot even when streaming. It’s a serious problem
So when I combine all of these thoughts together in my head. I actually just hope that this is an optics/display prototype being prepped for a bit later down the line. Rather than a Steam Deck/Steam Deck OLED situation
The software situation on Steam OS (for Frame) is still a mess. And to have valve engineers and contractors split between supporting two models THIS FAST, after such a rough launch, would be a bit of negligence, imo
At the end of the day, I knew valve would adopt Micro-OLED in one of their Headset products at some point. They’ve put serious effort into it over the past deckade and a half they’ve been doing VR. I’ve reported on some truly insane stuff they did in this field. It is inevitable
But for this, I pray that inevitability is a bit further out.. https://x.com/SadlyItsBradley/status/2110376728111534123/photo/1
tl;dr - I speculate the whole SM8650 board references to this is them just trying to prototype headsets with this optical stack based on what’s already lying around
Rather than them just.. building a whole module that is ready soon for mass production or whatever
